items.quote: What an epic game i must say, this is my second onimusha game after playing dawn of dreams all those years ago. Masterful combat and every moment in the fight is just epic. The sub characters are pretty interesting and musashi is a real one. The main villain himself is pretty menacing and deadly. There is a variety of mobs and bosses to fight against and some sub variation of them which i like a lot because they have different abilities. The visual is top notch as expected of RE engine and this being a more linear game. The soundtrack is pretty awesome as well. Very different to DOD and might give a bit of souls vibes but is actually pretty manageable at times. Definitely worth it at full price.

items.quote: After two decades of waiting, Capcom has finally brought back one of its most beloved franchises with Onimusha: Way of the Sword. This isn't just a simple nostalgic cash-grab; it is a complete, ground-up reinvention that successfully modernizes the classic samurai action for a new generation. **Story and Presentation**The game follows the journey of a young, cocky, yet highly skilled Miyamoto Musashi in feudal Kyoto. After acquiring the mysterious Oni Gauntlet, Musashi is thrust into a war against the demonic Genma. The narrative is engaging and well-paced, swapping between different character perspectives to keep the player hooked. What truly elevates the presentation is the outstanding character acting. The facial animations and voice acting are top-notch, perfectly capturing Musashi’s witty, sarcastic charm during intense showdowns. **Gameplay and Combat**Capcom has overhauled the gameplay entirely, abandoning the old tank controls and fixed camera angles in favor of fluid, dynamic movement. The combat feels heavy, deliberate, and incredibly fierce. Every sword strike carries immense weight. While it offers deep mechanical depth reminiscent of games like Nioh, it proudly stays true to its action roots rather than forcing itself into the modern "Soulslike" formula. For players struggling with the difficulty, the inclusion of an optional "Action Prompt" system helps teach defensive and counter-attack windows, making the game accessible without reducing the actual challenge. **Performance**True to Capcom's recent track record, the game runs beautifully. Visually, Kyoto looks stunning, and the performance is incredibly stable on both consoles and PC. Aside from minor frame drops when reloading saves—which are easily fixed—the optimization is practically flawless. **Verdict**Onimusha: Way of the Sword is an outstanding revival that honors its roots while bravely carving out a modern identity. With intense combat, an addictive gameplay loop, and excellent storytelling, Capcom has delivered yet another masterpiece in 2026.
